arguments.body: Hello, thank you for having us for the inspection. Two things came up that we'd like to check with you. 1) The inspector noted a dog flap fitted in the back door. Changes like this need the landlord's written consent under the alterations clause (and the pets clause) of your tenancy agreement. Did you get the landlord's consent? If so, please send us a copy or the date. 2) We've been told the front door lock may have been changed. Our records don't show this. Can you tell us who changed it and when? Please also let the agency have a copy of the new front door key by Sunday 25 February, so the landlord and agency have a spare for emergencies. Having a key does not give us a right to enter; we'll always give you 24 hours' written notice except in a genuine emergency. The inspector also noted marks from sticky strips on the Bedroom 1 wall by the window, which need to be removed and the wall made good. We'll update you by 26 February.

Our records do not show that consent was given for the dog flap, nor any lock change. We are asking the tenant today whether consent was given, who changed the lock and when, and for a copy of the new front door key to be given to the agency by 25 February. We will report back by 26 February. Please let us know whether you would consent to the dog flap, or want it removed, and whether you arranged or authorised any lock change.
